notes: Verified the new test really catches the bug: I re-applied only the handlerFor() extraction (no IsDir check) onto main in a scratch worktree and TestDirectoriesAreNotServedAsAssets fails with the actual FileServer directory listing ('<a href="index-DbG3xk91.js">'), while it passes on HEAD. go build ./..., go vet ./internal/web and go test ./... are all clean.

internal/web/web.go:44-52 error path is fine: f.Close() runs before the IsDir branch, so no file handle leaks when the entry is a directory or Stat fails; the statErr!=nil case falls through to the 404/SPA rules, which is the safe direction.

Behavior change worth knowing: directory paths (/assets, /assets/, /assets/chunks) now return 200 with the SPA index instead of a 301 to the trailing slash plus a listing. That follows the existing extensionless-route policy in web.go:53-59 and the commit message, but any external probe that expected 404/301 on /assets will now see 200 HTML. A directory whose name has an extension would now 404 instead of listing, which is the desired direction.

internal/web/web_test.go:41-62 (TestBundleFilesAreStillServed) would also pass on the pre-fix code — it is a regression guard, not proof of the fix. That is fine because TestDirectoriesAreNotServedAsAssets carries the proof.

Scope is tight: 2 files, +68/-3. The only refactor is extracting handlerFor(fs.FS) so the test can inject a fstest.MapFS standing in for a real Vite bundle (internal/web/dist only carries a placeholder index.html), which is necessary for testability. No auth/payment/migration/workflow/secret handling touched; pure in-process HTTP routing, trivially revertible.
